description: REGRESSION WALL: a `repcount` read DIRECTLY in an event-handler body is dispatch-dependent, so this program is CLEAN at `check()` (issue #1155). It looks like it should be a fault — there is no `repeat` anywhere — and an earlier draft of the rule reported it. The discriminating measurement uses this exact program, with NO `repeat` around the handler, so no enclosing construct could supply a turn: followed by `repeat 3 [ wait 1 ]` with the key delivered at tick 2 it PRINTS 2, the dispatching loop's second turn; followed by a bare `wait 3` it raises `ol-repcount-outside-repeat` at `runtime`. Same source, two outcomes, decided only by what is running when the key arrives — and the value 2 cannot be explained by any lexical reading. (An earlier draft cited `repeat 1 [ on_key … ] ` printing 1, which was inert: `repeat 1` has exactly one turn, so 1 is equally predicted by the hypothesis it was offered to refute. The tick was also unstated, and the value depends on it.) Reporting here would refuse a program that prints correctly, and since #815 put a severity gate in front of `execute()` that refusal blocks the run. This fixture fails the moment the rule judges a handler body lexically in EITHER direction — transparent or boundary — both of which report here; both directions were measured. The fault is not lost: it stays a `runtime` finding when the handler fires. What this does NOT license is treating a handler body as unknowable: see `check/repcount-in-procedure-inside-handler`, where a `define` inside this same body restores certainty and IS reported.
